On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. Shares are this community’s count divided by the New Westminster total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Uptown NW
Viceroy — 608 Belmont Street

A 24-storey, 188-unit concrete strata high-rise in Uptown at Belmont and Sixth, built in 2013 by Bosa Development; the property-manager building record gives strata plan EPS1234, freehold strata title, and amenities including a gym, hot tub, garden, storage lockers and underground parking. No source checked states any age restriction. Basis: property-manager building-data source, verified by name this pass. Counted: 1.
The Woodward — 612 Sixth Street

A strata high-rise (strata plan LMS3871) with direct internal access to Royal City Centre, managed by Quay Pacific Property Management; the building directory records it built in 1999, with bylaws of pets allowed with restrictions and "rentals not allowed" — that rental line is void province-wide since November 24, 2022. Unit count is not confirmed: the building directory's unit line conflicts with other directory figures for this address, so no count is stated. No source checked states any age restriction. Basis: property-manager welcome package (strata plan, mall access, manager) plus building-directory entry, verified by name this pass. Counted: 1.
258 Sixth Street ("258") — 258 Sixth Street

A 75-unit, 16-storey mixed-use high-rise developed by Tridecca, completed in 2014, with commercial units on the ground floor; current listings record its units as Apartment/Condo, freehold strata, in the Uptown NW sub-area. No source checked states any age restriction. Basis: developer project source plus name-verifying current listings. Counted: 1.
Amara Terrace — 1026 Queens Avenue

A 14-storey, 97-unit concrete strata high-rise at Queens and Eleventh, with a gym, pool, shared laundry and underground parking per the property-manager building record. Year built is not confirmed between sources: the property-manager record states 1985, while a current listing records 1984 — quote neither as settled. No source checked states any age restriction. Basis: property-manager building record plus name-verifying current listing. Counted: 1.
Queens Terrace — 1032 Queens Avenue / 1035 Auckland Street

A complex built in 1995; the building record lists pets allowed w/restrictions and rentals allowed w/restrictions — the rental-restriction element of that line is void since November 24, 2022, and the same record gives 104 units and amenities including an exercise centre and guest suite. No source checked states any age restriction. Basis: building-directory entry, verified by name this pass. Counted: 1.

Unit count: Not confirmed from the sources checked. No source checked states any age restriction. Basis: name-verifying current listings, consistent across units and brokerages. Counted: 1.
Penny Lane — 221 Ash Street

A small Uptown NW strata low-rise built in 1994: current listings name the complex "Penny Lane" at this address in Uptown NW. Unit count: Not confirmed from the sources checked. No source checked states any age restriction. Basis: name-verifying current listings. Counted: 1.
Streets, schools and getting around Uptown NW

items.t: Uptown is New Westminster's uphill commercial and civic core, centred on Sixth Street and Sixth Avenue above the Downtown waterfront, roughly between Royal Avenue / Sixth Avenue, Eighth Street and Tenth Street, taking in City Hall, the main public library, Moody Park's east edge and the Sixth Street shopping corridor. Exact board sub-area boundary roads are not verified.

Civic core: New Westminster City Hall is at 511 Royal Avenue at the south edge of the Uptown plateau, and the New Westminster Public Library Main Branch is at 716 6th Avenue inside the area. Royal City Centre, the enclosed mall at 610 Sixth Street, is the area's main shopping centre — over 40 shops and services (mall operator source, labelled as such).

Transit: there is no SkyTrain station inside Uptown; the nearest stations are New Westminster Station and Columbia Station (Expo Line) at the foot of the hill downtown. TransLink routes 105 (Uptown / New Westminster Station) and 106 (Edmonds Station / New Westminster Station) run through the Uptown corridors, and routes 103 and 123 also serve the Sixth Street / Sixth Avenue area.

Schools and catchments: SD40 catchments are address-based and do not follow neighbourhood lines, and every New Westminster student attends the district's single secondary school. A School Locator run for 835 Eighth Street returned Lord Kelvin Elementary, Fraser River Middle and New Westminster Secondary; a run for 1714 Eighth Avenue returned École Lord Tweedsmuir Elementary, Fraser River Middle and New Westminster Secondary. The replacement New Westminster Secondary School at 820 Sixth Street opened to students on January 11, 2021 — a $106.5 million, 1,900-seat building — and SD40's long-range facilities plan notes it is already operating above capacity. Check the exact address in the locator before relying on a school name.

Parks and recreation: Moody Park, at the area's northwest edge, has an outdoor pool, spray park and sports fields, and Moody Park Arena is at 701 8th Avenue. The təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre at 65 East Sixth Avenue, a short distance east of Uptown, fully opened in May 2024 — at 10,644 m² it is the City's largest capital project to date.
Health: the city's hospital is Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street in Sapperton, east of Uptown (Fraser Health).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Uptown NW

items.t: RT CORRECTION — required: The actual townhouse residential districts in Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 are RT-2, RT-2A, RT-2B, RT-2C and RT-3, RT-3A, RT-3B.

Heritage: the Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area sits just east of Uptown — Uptown itself is outside it, so heritage status here is property-by-property, checked against the City's heritage register rather than assumed from the neighbourhood.

blocks.text: Good to know about Uptown NW

items.t: One street, three buildings, one trap: on Queens Avenue, the subsidized seniors rental (Hillside Place, 1025) faces a general-market strata tower (Amara Terrace, 1026) directly across the street, and Queens Terrace (1032) stands on the same block. A search built on the name "Hillside" or the street alone will mix rental seniors housing with ordinary condos for sale — only 1025 is seniors housing, and it is rental.

There are two Hillside Places in the same small city, in different sub-areas. Hillside Place at 1025 Queens Avenue (Uptown) is non-profit seniors rental; Hillside Place at 509 Carnarvon Street (Downtown NW) is a general-market strata marketed to families and investors. A listing, a strata document or a showing booked under the bare name can belong to either — the street address is the only safe identifier.
The seven verified entries in are the corrected position.

Legion Manor's paper trail is dated by design. The City figure behind every published Legion Manor count — 123 units plus 6 wheelchair-accessible — comes from the City's 2009 Non-Market Housing Inventory.

The city's density is the context for every Uptown purchase. New Westminster counted 78,916 people in 2021 at 5,052 people per sq. km — the second-densest municipality in Canada — and Uptown is its Frequent Transit Development Area core, which is why a 1973 low-rise on Ash Street and a 2013 Bosa tower on Belmont Street sit in the same small sub-area and why the district's single secondary school, at 820 Sixth Street, is already above its 1,900-seat capacity.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Uptown NW
Streets, schools and getting around Uptown NW

items.t: Uptown is New Westminster's uphill commercial/civic core, centred on Sixth Street and Sixth Avenue above the Downtown waterfront, roughly between Royal Avenue / Sixth Avenue, Eighth and Tenth Streets, taking in City Hall (511 Royal Ave), the Main Library (716 6th Ave), Moody Park's east edge and Royal City Centre (610 Sixth St, 40+ shops, mall-operator source). Exact board boundary roads: Not verified.

Flood: the City floodplain study zones only the low edges — Zone 1 Queensborough, Zone 2 west-end industrial, Zone 3 Quay/Downtown NW, Zone 4 Brunette — no floodplain zone for the Uptown plateau was confirmed; lot-level status checked with the City.

Schools: SD40, address-based, one secondary school district-wide. Completed locator runs documented in this area's own research (2026-10-21): 835 Eighth Street → Lord Kelvin Elementary, Fraser River Middle, New Westminster Secondary; 1714 Eighth Avenue → École Lord Tweedsmuir Elementary, Fraser River Middle, New Westminster Secondary (Early French Immersion at Lord Tweedsmuir itself). The replacement NWSS at 820 Sixth Street opened Jan 11, 2021 ($106.5M, 1,900 seats) and is already above capacity per SD40's facilities plan. Other addresses: Not verified.

Transit/roads/health: no SkyTrain station in Uptown — nearest are New Westminster + Columbia stations downtown; routes 105, 106 (plus 103, 123) serve Sixth St/Sixth Ave. Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia St, Sapperton. Moody Park (pool, spray park, fields; Arena 701 8th Ave) and the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre, 65 East Sixth Ave (fully opened May 2024).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Uptown NW

items.t: Form B diligence (any Uptown strata, incl. Penny Lane): SPA s.59 — fees, amounts owing, approved special levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; rules, budget, Rental Disclosure Statement, most recent depreciation report attached; within 7 days, max $35 plus up to 25¢/page. In Uptown's older low-rise stock the depreciation report is the first-order document.

: OCP "Our City 2041," Bylaw No. 7925, 2017 — Uptown is a Frequent Transit Development Area (higher-density, transit-supportive growth directed to the Sixth St/Sixth Ave core; a planning direction, not a rezoning of any specific lot). RS-1 (s.310): min site 557.40 m², FSR 0.5; secondary suites allowed in RS, laneway/carriage houses regulated in the same bylaw. Heritage: Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area sits just east — Uptown itself is outside it, so heritage status is property-by-property.

blocks.text: Good to know about Uptown NW

items.t: Townhouse zoning: the newer RT-A and RT-B districts need at least 836.1 m² (9,000 sq. ft.) of site area, at least 20 m of frontage and lane access; the older districts are RT-2 to RT-2C and RT-3, RT-3A and RT-3B.
Uptown's attached depth is apartments, not townhouses. A "townhomes in Uptown" search mostly returns apartment units and one split-form low-rise (Penny Lane).

The city's only secondary school is already over capacity — NWSS (820 Sixth St, 1,900 seats, opened 2021) is above capacity in SD40's own facilities plan, which matters to every Uptown family purchase regardless of elementary catchment.

Legion Manor's counts are from 2009. Every published figure (123 + 6 accessible) traces to the City's 2009 Non-Market Housing Inventory — the current count is not confirmed; verify with the Royal City Legion Housing Society.

blocks.text: Uptown home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

125 condos sold in Uptown with a median price of $529,000 (the middle half sold between $405,000 and $627,500), taking a median of 25 days to sell at 97.0% of the last list price; 6% sold above list. They had a median $548 per square foot, a median year built of 1992 and a median strata fee of $572 a month. 10 townhomes sold in Uptown with a median price of $776,000 (the middle half sold between $678,500 and $894,375), taking a median of 15 days to sell at 98.0% of the last list price; 10% sold above list. They had a median $592 per square foot, a median year built of 1999 and a median strata fee of $616 a month.

faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 97 condos and townhomes listed in Uptown. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.
faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Uptown?

faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes in Uptown had a sales ratio of 24%, which the reports’ scale reads as a sellers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.
faq.q: Is Uptown a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?

faq.a: 81 condos and townhomes sold in Uptown over those 5 months, out of 327 in all of New Westminster.
faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Uptown from June to October 2026?

faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.
faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?

faq.a: Seven counted entries: Viceroy (608 Belmont St, 24 storeys, 188 units, 2013, Bosa), The Woodward (612 Sixth St, strata plan LMS3871), 258 Sixth Street (75 units, 16 storeys, 2014, Tridecca), Amara Terrace (1026 Queens Ave, 14 storeys, 97 units, year not confirmed 1984/1985), Queens Terrace (1032 Queens Ave / 1035 Auckland St, 1995), Ashington Court (425 Ash St, 1973) and Penny Lane (221 Ash St, 1994, form split in listings).
faq.q: Which condo buildings are verified by name in Uptown NW?

faq.a: No. The nearest stations are New Westminster Station and Columbia Station (Expo Line), downtown at the foot of the hill; TransLink routes 105 and 106 connect Uptown to the stations, and routes 103 and 123 also serve the Sixth Street / Sixth Avenue area. Test the hill walk from the specific building to its bus stop before buying.
faq.q: Is there a SkyTrain station in Uptown?

faq.a: The Woodward (612 Sixth Street, strata plan LMS3871) has direct internal access to Royal City Centre (610 Sixth Street, over 40 shops and services) — the strata's own manager welcome package and the building's listings both state the inside connection. It is still a general-market strata with no age bylaw, and its directory "rentals not allowed" line is void province-wide.
faq.q: What is The Woodward's mall access?

faq.a: Yes. The Uptown one, at 1025 Queens Avenue, is a non-profit seniors rental (16 homes, Housing Registry). The other, at 509 Carnarvon Street, is a general-market strata in Downtown NW. Same name, different building, different sub-area — and the strata tower across the street from the Uptown rental, at 1026 Queens Avenue, is a third building again: Amara Terrace, general-market.
faq.q: Are there really two buildings called Hillside Place?

faq.a: Its listings split: one unit is filed Apartment, another Row/Townhouse and marketed as a townhome. It is counted once, in condos, on the apartment-listing evidence with the split stated — documented here, never double-counted. Buy/title it as the strata low-rise it is and settle form from the strata plan/Form B.
faq.q: Is Penny Lane a townhouse complex?

faq.a: Short-term rentals can still be restricted.
faq.q: Can I rent out an Uptown strata long-term?

faq.a: Not by default. RT-A and RT-B are the newer townhouse districts (at least 836.1 m² (9,000 sq. ft.) of site area, at least 20 m of frontage and lane access) and apply only to lots the City designates or rezones for townhouses; check the lot's zoning with City Planning.
faq.q: RT-A/RT-B — is that Uptown townhouse zoning?
What did condos in Uptown sell for?
faq.a: 125 condos sold in Uptown between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $529,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Uptown?
faq.a: The median was 25 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.0% of the last list price (6% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
